text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the volunteer mentor team of the Puentes de Luz Scholarship Fund in the Valle Serrano district. This guide explains how you will support the 240 girls currently enrolled in lower and upper secondary schools. Each mentor is assigned up to six scholars and should meet them at least twice a month. In 2023, scholars who met their mentor regularly had an attendance rate of 91 percent. Mentors do not handle scholarship payments; these are sent directly to schools by the finance office. If a scholar misses more than three consecutive days, call her guardian before contacting the head teacher. Never promise a girl additional funds, as stipends are fixed by the committee each January. Record every visit in the green logbook so that coordinators can track progress across all fourteen partner schools.

variants.whitespace_case: this guide explains how you will support the 240 GIRLS currently enrolled in lower and upper secondary schools.

variants.added_negation: This guide does not explain how you will support the 240 girls currently enrolled in lower and upper secondary schools.
variants.removed_negation: Mentors handle scholarship payments; these are sent directly to schools by the finance office.
variants.reordered: If a scholar misses more than three consecutive days, call the head teacher before contacting her guardian.
variants.paraphrase: Girls who saw their mentors consistently attended school 91 percent of the time in 2023.

passages.source_passage: Board Update, Quarter Three: The Open Paths Accessibility Project in Marrowfield County has now distributed 1,150 assistive devices, including wheelchairs, hearing aids and white canes, since its launch in March 2022. Ramp construction at 18 primary schools was completed in August, two weeks ahead of schedule. However, the planned audit of public clinics did not begin, because the county health office has not yet signed the access agreement. Device users reported a 64 percent improvement in their ability to reach markets independently. Staff trained forty local technicians to repair wheelchairs, which reduces waiting times considerably. The board is asked to approve a reallocation of 12 percent of the transport budget toward a mobile repair van. No additional funds are requested at this stage.

passages.source_passage: Background and Need: Kelvara Camp, located 35 kilometres from the Tamsin border crossing, hosts approximately 48,000 refugees, of whom 52 percent are children. The Haven Rights Collective has provided case management in the camp since 2019, focusing on unaccompanied minors, survivors of violence and older persons living alone. In the last twelve months, caseworkers registered 2,300 new protection cases, yet only nine caseworkers are currently employed. As a result, many families did not receive a follow-up visit within the required 14 days. Referral pathways to legal aid exist, but they are not consistently used because transport to the district court is unavailable. This proposal seeks funding to recruit six additional caseworkers and establish a weekly mobile legal clinic inside the camp.

passages.source_passage: Board Update – Coastal Alert Programme, November 2024. The Saltmere Resilience Trust has installed 27 siren towers along the Brackwater coastline, covering an estimated 61,000 residents. During the October drill, 83 percent of households in pilot villages reached evacuation points within thirty minutes. The SMS warning system, however, did not perform as expected: messages reached only half of registered phones because two network masts were offline. Village volunteers alerted elderly residents door to door, and no injuries were reported. Management recommends signing a backup agreement with a second mobile operator before the cyclone season begins in April. The board should note that the programme is not yet covering the four island communities, which remain accessible only by boat.

passages.source_passage: Board Update: Little Steps Playgroup Network. Since January 2023, the Ferngate Family Foundation has opened 32 community playgroups across the Ollan Hills, each meeting three mornings a week. Around 780 children aged two to five now attend regularly. Developmental screening in June found that 72 percent of children met age-appropriate language milestones, compared with 55 percent at baseline. Parent volunteers lead most sessions, supported by eight paid facilitators. Not every site has suitable space; five playgroups still meet outdoors and cannot operate during heavy rain. We did not reach our target of enrolling 1,000 children, mainly because two planned sites lost their venues. The board is invited to discuss whether to prioritise covered shelters over expansion in the coming year.

passages.source_passage: Annual Report to the Brightwater Foundation, 2023–2024. Over the reporting year, Clearspring Rural Water drilled 14 new boreholes in the Duvan and Petrel sub-counties, giving an estimated 9,600 people access to safe water within 500 metres of their homes. Communities built 410 household latrines with materials subsidised by the project. Open defecation was not eliminated in any village, although three communities are expected to be certified by mid-2025. Water committees collected user fees in 11 of the 14 sites, covering roughly 60 percent of routine maintenance costs. One borehole in Kessa failed a water quality test in February and has not been reopened. Women now spend about forty minutes less per day collecting water, according to the household survey.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer Trainer Notes: Week One. The Northgate Skills Centre in Ravensholt offers six-month courses in electrical installation, tailoring and motorcycle repair to young people aged 17 to 24. Each cohort has a maximum of 20 trainees, and you will co-teach with a qualified instructor. Last year, 68 percent of graduates found paid work or started a business within six months of finishing. Do not allow trainees to operate power tools until they have passed the safety quiz on day three. Trainees who miss more than four sessions in a month are referred to the youth counsellor, not dismissed. Volunteers should never lend money to trainees, even small amounts for transport. Please submit attendance sheets to the front office every Friday by 4 p.m.

passages.source_passage: Mid-Term Evaluation Summary: Safe Arrivals Outreach, Barhali District. The evaluation team visited 12 of the 20 health posts supported by the Sundara Health Alliance between September and October 2024. Facility births in the catchment area rose from 46 percent at baseline to 63 percent, exceeding the mid-term target. Community health workers completed an average of three antenatal home visits per pregnant woman. However, postnatal checks within 48 hours were not consistently recorded, and the team could not verify the reported figure of 70 percent. Stock-outs of oxytocin occurred at four health posts during the monsoon. Mothers interviewed praised the outreach workers, but several said they never received the promised transport voucher. The evaluators recommend a simplified postnatal register and quarterly supply reviews.

passages.source_passage: Guide for Volunteer Listeners, Calmwater Community Counselling. Our service in the Hollin Estate offers free, confidential support sessions to adults experiencing stress, grief or low mood. Each volunteer completes 30 hours of training before seeing clients and attends supervision once every two weeks. A typical session lasts fifty minutes, and clients may attend up to eight sessions. You are not a therapist, and you should never offer a diagnosis or advice on medication. If a client mentions thoughts of self-harm, stop the session plan and contact the duty supervisor immediately. In 2024, around 85 percent of clients said they felt listened to. Do not share client details with anyone outside the supervision team, including family members who call on the client's behalf.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer Briefing: Harvest Bridge Cash Assistance. The Amberly Relief Network provides monthly cash transfers of 45 dollars to 3,200 households in the drought-affected Sorrel Plains. Transfers are sent by mobile money on the fifth of each month, from May to December 2025. Your role is to help households register, check their identity documents and explain how to withdraw funds. You must not tell recipients how to spend the money; the programme is unconditional. Households headed by women make up 58 percent of the caseload. If a recipient says a payment has not arrived, record the phone number and report it to the hotline within two days. Never collect a recipient's PIN or hold their SIM card, even if they ask you to.
